record.name: Wuliangshan Gushu Shou
record.origin: Wuliang Mountain, Jingdong County, Pu'er City, Yunnan, China

paragraphs.text: A cake of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Wuliang Mountain, in Jingdong County, Pu'er City, pressed in 2019. Before pressing, the leaf was heaped warm and damp in a [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling), the method Yunnan's state factories brought into production in 1973, and then dried.
At seven years it has entered the stretch between five and ten, when the [mark of the pile](shou:age-settling) has usually worn off and the tea has had time to settle.

brewing.text: From a cake, brick or tuo, ease a piece off along the edge with a pick rather than snapping it, so the leaves stay whole. Ripe pu’er takes boiling water and forgives a heavy hand. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens; it gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, sweet cup with earthy or woody notes. A young ripe tea can carry a faint smell of the pile, which fades with airing or in the first steeps.
